statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). NQ trades at 29,450.50, unchanged on the day, inside the same 68-point Globex band from 29,426.75 to 29,495.25 that has held since the 22:00 UTC reopen. The marginal high printed an hour ago at 29,495.25 was not extended and price has returned toward mid-band, so Tail holds at 14. Stress remains high at 66: WTI is extending at 102.81 with the Saudi East-West pipeline still shut, the 10-year holds 4.961% after Monday's 5.012% print was rejected, and a two-day Federal Reserve meeting opens today.
recommendation: Tail at 14 sits in the low band, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The mean-reversion record across this window now spans five independent observations: Monday's cash index recovered 259.5 points off its 28,867.67 low, the 10-year's move above 5% was rejected and closed at 4.961%, Tokyo turned a lower open into a 64,082 print 1,015 points above its low, NQ's marginal Globex high was rejected an hour ago, and that high has not been retested since. Stress remains high at 66 because the energy and long-yield backdrop is unresolved, but Stress alone does not change the mapped state. The narrow danger window from 13:00 to 15:00 UTC covers the US cash open and the first full cash hour, the two intervals where an unretraced opening continuation would be most likely to appear.
headline: NQ holds a 68-point Globex band at 29,450 and leaves its marginal high unretested while Tokyo runs to 64,082; crude extends to $102.81 with the Saudi pipeline shut and the 10-year holds 4.961% as a two-day Fed meeting opens - Tail holds 14 with Stress high at 66
body:
The current hour rests on live evidence rather than an evidence gap, and that evidence continues to favour the mean-reversion reading. CME equity index futures have traded since the 22:00 UTC reopen inside a band 68.5 points wide, from 29,426.75 to 29,495.25, and NQ is currently 29,450.50 against a 29,449.50 previous close, a change of 0.00%. Roughly five and a half hours of containment inside a 0.23% range is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency that defines a pathological path. The specific development of this hour is what did not happen: the marginal new high at 29,495.25 that printed in the previous hour has not been retested, and price has instead settled back toward the middle of the band. A failed extension that is then left alone is stronger evidence than the failure itself, because it shows no second attempt was financed.

Cross-asset evidence is genuinely split, which is why the dominant mode is mixed rather than directional. Tokyo is trending: the Nikkei is 64,082.36, up 0.93%, having recovered 1,015 points from its 63,067.18 session low and trading near its 64,101.00 high. NQ is not following that strength, and a regional index trending while the Nasdaq complex sits flat is a divergence that argues against reading either as a global one-way impulse. Monday's US cash session tells the same split story. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,127.16, down 0.82%, but the path matters more than the close: the index traded down to 28,867.67 and recovered 259.5 points into the bell. Beneath the index the session was a rotation rather than a liquidation, with the PHLX chip index down 5.9% after the leaders of several AI laboratories warned publicly about the pace of development, while software and communications names closed higher. Conflicting breadth of that kind reduces directional conviction and belongs in Stress, not in Tail.

The stress backdrop is unresolved and severe, which is why Stress holds at 66 while Tail sits at 14. WTI is 102.81, up 1.40%, and Brent is 106.90. The Saudi East-West pipeline, which had been carrying four to five million barrels a day as the principal bypass for a Strait of Hormuz that has been closed since March, remains shut after the drone strikes of 11 September, with no stated restart date. The long end reflects that: the 10-year printed 5.012% on Monday, the first move above 5% since 2023, and was rejected back to 4.961%, while the VIX rose 7.95% to 17.10 on the session. A two-day Federal Reserve meeting opens today with the decision and press conference on Wednesday, and the Bank of Japan concludes its own meeting on Friday. That stack is a real hazard to a basket, and it is precisely the combination this assessment records as a Stress and Confidence input until an observed price path establishes that retracement has actually stopped occurring.

The conditional forward path therefore keeps Tail in the low band through the remainder of the Asian session and the European handover, enters the watch band across the European mid-morning hours that produced Monday's chip-led leg, and peaks at 23 across the declared 13:00 to 15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open and the first full cash hour. A secondary lift to 22 covers the 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC, where a weak result would pair a rate impulse with the existing energy shock. Every one of those elevations is a scheduled checkpoint rather than observed structure. The condition that would change the assessment is specific and currently absent: shallow or absent pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, and NQ holding near a session extreme rather than returning to the middle of its range.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments are available. Tail entered the window at 20, held a 19 to 23 range through the Asian session and the European handover, peaked at 26 during the European mid-morning chip-led decline and repeated 25 in the following hour, eased through midday, printed 26 again at the US cash open, then decayed steadily through the afternoon and evening to a 14 to 16 plateau across the last six hours as the opening decline was partly recovered. Stress fell from a 79 peak to 65 and 66, and Confidence held between 86 and 89 throughout. The window contains three hours in the orange band, all of them tied to the chip-led decline, and no hour reached the red band.
outlookSummary: The conditional path holds the low band through the remainder of the Asian session at 14 and 15, lifts to 17 for the European opening auction and 19 at the European cash open, enters the watch band at 21 across the two European mid-morning hours that produced Monday's chip-led leg, eases to 20 through the midday lull, returns to 21 for the 12:15 and 12:30 UTC releases, and peaks at 23 across the 13:00 to 15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open and the first full cash hour. It eases to 21 and 20 through the US midday, lifts to 22 for the 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC, holds 21 through the post-auction reaction and the power hour, and returns to the low band at 19 for the cash close. It falls to 16 inside the futures maintenance halt, recovers to 17 across the Globex reopen and the early Asian hours, and settles at 16 into the final pre-decision hours. Stress tracks a 66 to 75 path with its peak inside the danger window, and Confidence decays from 88 to 77 with forecast horizon.
